title: Staffage
description: Handcrafted architectural staffage with real dimensions, rigs, poses, clips, individually authored drawing-scale representations, layered thermal models, respiration and structural models. A document is an asset file, the manifest, the print profile document or the environment document.

Slug.description: A kebab-case identifier, unique within its scope.

Text.description: A human-readable text in every supported language; there is no default language.

CategoryId.description: One of the nine archive categories.

ParameterSource.description: How a physical parameter is known.

Viewpoint.description: The projection an asset is drawn in: the side elevation (the rig plane, seen from the right of the asset), the front elevation (seen from ahead), the plan (top view, seen from above), or the axonometric view of the 3D volumes; only the first three have authored shapes, the axonometric view is derived from `volumes`.

ExportFormat.description: The output kinds an asset can be exported to; glb is a glTF 2.0 binary with every pose and clip, fbx an FBX 7.4 binary of one clip, model the engine-neutral JSON model document, model-zip the ZIP of every pose and clip of an asset as glb, fbx and model files.

Completion.description: How far an asset has come.

Reference.description: A source a parameter or a shape relies on.

Provenance.description: Who made an asset and how.

PhaseChange.description: A phase change at constant temperature: the temperature of a heated region is capped at pointC and the surplus power is converted into mass of the new phase at latentHeatJKg.

Material.description: A material with the properties the thermal and structural models read.

JointType.description: How a bone may move relative to its parent.

Joint.description: A joint and its limits; revolute limits are angle offsets from rest, prismatic limits are offsets along axisDeg.

continuousTwist.description: A shaft bearing whose sole degree of freedom is unlimited rotation about its local longitudinal axis, expressed by twistDeg. A looping clip may close an integer number of full axial turns away.

SegmentMass.description: A segment mass: point mass at the local centre, or spread uniformly along the bone.

Bone.description: A rigid frame placed at (x, y, z) in its parent's frame and oriented in it at rest by angleDeg about the parent joint axis w, then abductionDeg about its own normal v, then twistDeg about its own axis u. A pose or clip offset then turns the bone about its own rest axes in the same order.

abductionDeg.description: Rest rotation about the bone's own normal v, applied after angleDeg: positive turns the bone axis u towards the joint axis w of the parent (the left of the asset for a sagittal parent). 90 lays a bone laterally: a clavicle, a pelvis half, an axle, a handlebar. Default 0.

twistDeg.description: Rest roll about the bone's own axis u, applied after angleDeg and abductionDeg: positive turns the normal v away from the joint axis w (v to -w, w to v). It sets the joint axis w of the bone, about which angleDeg offsets turn it and in whose frame its children are placed. Default 0.

Rig.description: A transform hierarchy with exactly one root.

radialFolds.description: Ordered pairs of terminal facet frames share a crown. The total angle of the flat fabric fixes the width of each pleat.

Anchor.description: A point fixed on a bone (local coordinates).

z.description: Lateral position in the bone frame (left is +); default 0.

tiltDeg.description: Elevation of the support normal out of the sagittal (x, y) plane towards the left (+z), degrees: 0 keeps the normal in the plane (the default), 90 points it along +z, so a roller with tiltDeg 90 restrains the lateral direction only (a lateral guide); the normal is (cos normalDeg cos tiltDeg, sin normalDeg cos tiltDeg, sin tiltDeg).

ShapeRole.description: The line-hierarchy role of a shape.

CapsuleShape.description: A stadium between two local points with radii r0 and r1 (tangent hull of two circles).

followTip.description: Plan geometry only: the (x1, y1) end follows the x travel of the tip of the shape's own bone while the (x0, y0) end follows its origin, so the stadium stretches along a limb seen from above.

RectShape.description: A rectangle with optional corner radius, lower-left at (x, y).

followTip.description: Front geometry only: the shape stretches vertically between the origin and the tip of its own bone; a vertex at the height of the bone origin follows the y travel of the origin and one at the height of the bone tip the y travel of the tip, in between linearly.

PolyShape.description: A polygon or polyline through local points. A closed polygon is filled even-odd: where it crosses itself the region wound an even number of times is a hole.

followTip.description: Front geometry only: the shape stretches vertically between the origin and the tip of its own bone; a vertex at the height of the bone origin follows the y travel of the origin and one at the height of the bone tip the y travel of the tip, in between linearly.

PathShape.description: An SVG-style path (M L H V C Q A Z, absolute or relative) in local metres, y up. Every subpath is a ring of the shape and a filled path is painted even-odd: a subpath inside another is a hole, and subpaths that overlap each other leave the overlap unpainted, so separate parts are separate shapes.

Solid.description: How a shape of any viewpoint (side elevation, front elevation or plan) is a solid of the rig plane profile, authored in its bone's local frame like a side elevation shape, placed with the full 3D frame of its bone and projected to the viewpoint; the side elevation, the front elevation and the plan of one solid are one 3D definition. revolved: an axisymmetric part about an axis through the rest origin of axisBone, the axis point is the rest origin of axisBone translated by axisX along world x and axisZ along world z at rest, and the axis is then carried with the bone frame; axisBone must be the shape's own bone or one of its ancestors, so the solid moves rigidly with its bone; front paper x is the lateral distance from the axis (mirror also draws the reflection, so a half profile reads as the whole body), plan is the circle of the widest lateral reach about the axis. extruded: a laterally prismatic part spanning z0..z1 (left is +); front is z0..z1 by the height range of the profile, plan is the forward range of the profile by z0..z1.

axisBone.description: The bone whose frame carries the axis: the shape's own bone or one of its ancestors (validator `solid-axis-not-ancestor`).

axis.description: The direction of the axis in the bone-local frame of axisBone: u along the bone, v its normal in the sagittal plane, w the lateral axis (left is +). The axis is carried with the bone frame, so the solid revolves about the same line whatever the pose. Axisymmetric parts about a vertical bone use u; a part about a horizontal axle across the bone uses w.

axisX.description: Translation of the axis point from the rest origin of axisBone along the world x axis (ahead) at rest, not along the bone's u; the axis is then carried with the bone frame.

axisZ.description: Translation of the axis point from the rest origin of axisBone along the world z axis (left is +) at rest, not along the bone's w; default 0; the axis is then carried with the bone frame.

lateralScale.description: Optional elliptic cross-section: the scale of the radius along the bone axis u projected perpendicular to the revolve axis (along w when the axis is parallel to u, the kernel semantics) relative to the radius in the profile; 1 is a physical circle (the default, not a fallback), 0.5 an ellipse half as wide as it is deep.

weights.description: Blend of the solid over bones (skinning): at most four influences, each a bone and a non-negative weight, summing to 1 (validators `volume-weights-bone` and `volume-weights-sum`); absent: the solid is rigid to `bone`. The coordinates stay those of the frame of `bone`.

sweep.description: Required bone-local axis of extrusion. For u the profile coordinates are (v, w), for v they are (u, w), and for w they are (u, v). z0 and z1 span the named axis. A length on u or v is relative to the bone origin. Lateral w extents are measured in world z at rest.

zTip.description: Optional linear taper: the lateral span [z0, z1] (left is +) at the tip of the bone, in the same order as z0..z1 (zTip[0] < zTip[1]); the span at the bone origin is z0..z1 and the span between is interpolated linearly along the first profile coordinate, normalized by bone length (u for v and w sweeps, v for a u sweep). Absent means a constant span. A tapered limb, blade or branch is one extruded solid.

Shape.description: An authored shape of one representation, bound to a bone: one geometry plus the common fields. region binds one thermal region, regions a merged form; hatch names a hatch of the representation; penMm overrides the pen of the role. Fill rule (one for every filled shape, every renderer and every check): even-odd. A point is inside when a ray from it crosses the rings of the shape an odd number of times, whatever their winding, so a ring inside another is a hole and the overlap of two rings of one shape is a hole too; a shape whose parts overlap is therefore drawn as separate shapes (or as their union outline), never as overlapping subpaths.

followTip.description: Front geometry only: the shape stretches vertically between the origin and the tip of its own bone; a vertex at the height of the bone origin follows the y travel of the origin and one at the height of the bone tip the y travel of the tip, in between linearly.

Front geometry only: the shape stretches vertically between the origin and the tip of its own bone; a vertex at the height of the bone origin follows the y travel of the origin and one at the height of the bone tip the y travel of the tip, in between linearly.

oneOf.description: A member: a prismatic bar between two bone-local end points with a physical section, carried by the full 3D frames of its bones and drawn in its true foreshortened outline in every viewpoint. It has no planar geometry and no solid; a diagonal is one member and never a bounding rectangle.

ScaleBands.description: The denominator band [from, to] each preset scale stands for; together they tile the promised drawing range 1:20…1:1000 without a hole. The validRanges of an asset's authored representations must cover the union of the bands of its authored presets without a hole (rule valid-range-gap): the boundary between two authored neighbours may move, the outer ends may not shrink.

PenSet.description: The pens of a representation per role in paper millimetres; null means the role is not drawn.

Hatch.description: A hatch drawn inside shapes that name it: spacing and pen in paper millimetres.

RepresentationDecisions.description: The authored design decisions of one representation.

AuthoredRepresentation.description: A representation individually authored for one preset scale.

validRange.description: The range of custom denominators this representation is validated for (it contains its own denominator and prints over its whole range). The ranges of all authored representations of an asset cover the ScaleBands of its authored presets without a hole.

sections.description: Which of the three projections, the side elevation, the front elevation or the plan (top view), is drawn as a section.

ViewSection.description: A viewpoint drawn as a section: the cut plane lies at `plane` metres along the view axis (elevation: the lateral position z of a vertical plane along the forward axis, seen from the right, the part at smaller z removed; front: the forward position x of a plane across the forward axis, seen from ahead, the part at larger x removed; plan: the height y of a horizontal plane, seen from above, the part above removed; the plan section is named Grundriss-Schnitt in German) and is named by `label`, such as A-A. The side elevation shows the cut-line marker of a front or plan section, the plan the cut-line marker of an elevation section.

retained.description: Which half of the body the section view shows, seen from the viewpoint: `far` (default) the half behind the plane, the conventional section (elevation: larger z, front: smaller x, plan: lower y); `near` the half in front of it. A hollow part of the shown half is drawn as a filled closed shape with its bore as a hole.

Alternative.description: What to offer instead of an unavailable representation.

UnavailableRepresentation.description: An explicit decision that the asset cannot be meaningfully drawn at this scale.

cause.description: Why no physically scaled drawing exists at this scale, in all three viewpoints: a real feature is smaller than the print profile can print (`below-printable-feature`) or the asset has no meaningful physical depiction at this scale (`no-physical-depiction`).

Representation.description: The decision for one preset scale.

SymbolRepresentation.description: A conventional symbol, separately identified from the pictorial representations.

PrintProfile.description: A print profile: smallest stroke, gap, feature width and hatch spacing that reliably print.

BoneOffset.description: An offset from rest for one bone, applied after its rest placement about the bone's own rest axes: angleDeg about its joint axis w, then abductionDeg about its normal v, then twistDeg about its axis u. abductionDeg is the lateral spread of a revolute bone: the bone turns out of its rest plane about its own normal (positive towards its joint axis: the left of the asset for a sagittal bone); all three views are projections of the same three-dimensional chain. twistDeg turns the bone and its subtree about its own longitudinal axis (a yaw for a vertical bone: slew, swivel, steering). Children ride on the offset bone.

twistDeg.description: Axial rotation in degrees. The bone limits ordinary joints. A continuous shaft may turn freely.

AppliedLoad.description: A load applied at an anchor or a bone point, in world newtons.

z.description: Lateral position of the load point (left is +) for a bone point; default 0.

momentXNm.description: Moment about the forward axis; default 0.

momentYNm.description: Moment about the vertical axis; default 0.

momentNm.description: Moment about the lateral axis (the sagittal moment, counter-clockwise positive in the elevation); default 0.

RegionBinding.description: The region state a pose binds.

ThermalBinding.description: The thermal and respiratory state a pose or clip key binds explicitly.

Pose.description: A named configuration or an in-between key pose of a clip.

Ease.description: How a key eases into the next one. linear, in (t^2), out (1-(1-t)^2) and step blend the two key states by the eased weight; smooth is a C1 cubic Hermite (Catmull-Rom) segment through the neighbouring keys: tangents are the finite differences across the previous and next key (wrapping for looping clips, zero at the ends of non-looping clips), angles in degrees on bone offsets, translations linear in value space, so velocity is continuous across keys. Scalar tracks follow the same rule. Looping clips drop a last key at or beyond the duration that repeats the first.

ContactSpan.description: A time span during which an anchor is in contact.

ClipEvent.description: A point event on the clip timeline.

ScalarTrack.description: A scalar track of a clip.

Clip.description: A deterministic clip over named poses.

fps.description: Frames per second of the clip, any positive number: a slow thermal transient of hours is sampled with a fractional rate (0.01 is one frame per 100 s).

windDirectionDeg.description: Horizontal bearing the air moves towards, degrees from the forward axis +x towards the left axis +z (0 forward, 90 towards the left of the asset, 180 backward; the frame is left-handed: x ahead, y up, z left); the wind has no vertical component.

ThermalModelKind.description: How a region's surface temperature is obtained.

ThermalLayer.description: One layer of a region, innermost first.

ThermalRegion.description: A thermal region: one surface patch with its layers and model parameters.

areaBasis.description: The area represented by areaM2. By default it is the outer surface in the assembly. Total is the component's complete outer area before other components cover it, with the pose's exposedFraction controlling the area available for heat exchange. Exchange is the effective leaf, fur, feather or hair area. Total and default areas are measured against geometry. Leaf models and foliage, fur, feather and hair regions require exchange.

heatW.description: Heat released inside the surface at operating level 1, in watts; signed: a negative value removes heat (an evaporator, a cooling coil, a chilled surface) and the level may be negative for a reversed duty.

ratedPowerW.description: Nameplate power in watts of the element this region represents, stated once per element, on any region; the source and reference of the region cover it. The total power of an asset is the sum of these ratings plus the metabolic heat of its bodies, never derived from operating.heatW (released heat).

ratedPowerBasis.description: What the rating states: electrical-input (appliances, devices, lamps, heat pumps: input, not capacity), fuel-input (burners and fires), rated-output (engines, traction and drive motors, generating sets) or passive (the element draws nothing: 0 W).

BodyPhysiology.description: The whole-body thermal physiology of a human or animal.

BreathingPattern.description: A breathing pattern: frequency, tidal volume and the split of one cycle into four phases.

Emitter.description: A rig-attached source of air or vapour. A vent, flue, fan or exhaust with a region releases the vapour mass rate of that region's evaporation (surface evaporation plus phase change).

Passenger.description: A second living body carried by the asset.

OperatingKey.description: An operating state family of a machine.

ThermalModel.description: The thermal model of an asset.

minimumAirPassageM.description: Width in metres of the smallest modeled opening that connects a heat-exchange surface to outside air.

referenceEnvironment.description: The ambient case standalone thermal previews and exports use by default: the id of an environment preset or one inline environment. An explicit choice of the caller wins; absent, `environment` applies.

Vector2.description: Two numbers [a, b]: a coordinate pair in the plane of a profile, in metres.

Vector3.description: Three numbers [u, v, w]: a point or direction in the bone-local frame, in metres for points.

Quaternion.description: A rotation quaternion [x, y, z, w] of unit length (validator `volume-transform`); the identity is [0, 0, 0, 1].

VolumeTransform.description: An optional placement of one volume solid inside the bone-local frame, applied to the solid's own coordinates in the order scale, rotation, translation; each part absent means identity. scale is a per-axis scale about the bone-local origin of the solid (u, v, w; every factor positive), rotation a unit quaternion about that origin, translation in metres.

VolumeRepeat.description: Repeats a volume solid as `count` copies; copy k (k = 0 .. count-1) is the solid after `transform`, moved by the step applied k times: first the rotation of k * rotationRad about the axis rotationAxis through the point origin (default [0, 0, 0]), then k * translation. count is at least 1 and at most 256 (validator `volume-repeat`); absent rotationRad, rotationAxis or translation mean no rotation or no translation. Copies inherit every other field of the solid, including its weights.

VolumeSolid.description: One declarative solid of one list of a scale volume (body, thermal or structure), bound to a bone of the rig. Coordinates are metres in the rest frame of `bone`: the origin is the bone origin (including the bone's own lateral offset z), u runs along the bone from its joint towards its tip, v is its normal in the sagittal plane (the local y of an elevation shape, u turned by +90 degrees counter-clockwise in the side elevation) and w is lateral (left of the asset is +, world z at rest); this is the frame of the elevation shapes (x = u, y = v) and of the `solid` hints. The pose of the bone carries the solid: it follows the rig through every pose and clip. Six kinds: box (centred axis-aligned box with optionally rounded edges), ellipsoid (centred ellipsoid with the semi-axes along u, v, w), capsule (hull of two spheres, optionally elliptic), revolve (a profile of [axial, radial] revolved about an axis), extrude (a polygon with holes on a coordinate plane pushed along the third axis, optionally tapered) and loft (superelliptic sections joined in order). transform places the solid, then repeat copies it. Every size and radius is positive and every profile is a simple polygon A solid of the body list is exactly this; thermal and structural solids add the fields of ThermalSolid and StructuralSolid (validators `volume-size`, `volume-profile-degenerate`, `volume-profile-self-intersecting`, `volume-hole-outside`, `volume-holes-overlap`, `volume-extrude-range`, `volume-loft-sections`).

oneOf.description: A box centred on the origin of the bone-local frame with edges along u, v, w; size is the edge length along u, v, w; cornerRadius rounds every edge and is at most half the smallest edge.

id.description: Unique among the solids of its list at this scale (validator `volume-duplicate-id`).

bone.description: The bone whose rest frame carries the coordinates of this solid and which the solid follows rigidly unless `weights` blend it (validator `volume-bone`).

material.description: The id of an entry of the asset's `materials` that colours and, in the thermal view, binds the solid (validator `volume-material`).

role.description: The line-hierarchy role of the solid in the line views: body for the main mass, detail for small parts, texture, glazing for transparent parts, ground for contact surfaces.

tone.description: The grey tone 0 (black) to 1 (white) the solid takes in the solid views of the dark and light themes, like the tone of a shape.

weights.description: Blend of the solid over bones (skinning): at most four influences, each a bone and a non-negative weight, summing to 1 (validators `volume-weights-bone` and `volume-weights-sum`); absent: the solid is rigid to `bone`. The coordinates stay those of the frame of `bone`.

tags.description: Free labels of the solid; the label `glyph` is reserved for generated analysis glyphs.

sectionFaces.description: Faces of this solid that are section cuts through a continuing construction (a wall, slab or beam sample) or the hidden back of a one-sided patch: every face whose outward normal lies within 45 degrees of one of these bone axes (`-u`, `+u`, `-v`, `+v`, `-w`, `+w` of the solid's bone frame) counts for no thermal area and is drawn as a cut face.

slender.description: Declares a slender part (cord, wire, capillary, rod, hose, antenna): its length is at least 20 times its largest cross extent (validator `volumes-slender`); a `member` solid of the `structure` list (a bone, a strut) may declare it from 5 times and a length of two smallest features of the scale. A slender solid is exempt from `volumes-feature` and from the cross-scale comparison; at each scale it is as thick as that scale's 2D draws it, and a coarser scale may keep it in `thermal` or `structure` without having it in `body`.

sheet.description: Declares a true thin sheet (feather vane, leaf blade, fabric, membrane, foil, sheet metal, thin board or panel, thin vessel or shell wall built as a plate): it keeps its physical thickness below the smallest feature of the scale when its middle extent is at least that feature and at least 20 times its thickness (validator `volumes-feature`); where a thermal layer declares a gauge (`thicknessM`) for its bone and material, the thickness is that gauge. Not together with `slender`. A lump or a strip is no sheet.

envelope.description: Marks an envelope solid: at a coarser scale a lattice (truss, mast, framework) of the finer scale is replaced by its envelope prism, or a row of many thin elements (balusters, pales, louvres) by fewer, thicker ones on a bone of their own (typification), declared in `decisions`; cross-scale then compares the convex hull of the envelope solids of a bone with the convex hull of the finer solids of that bone instead of part against part (validator `volume-envelope`: not at the finest authored scale).

texture.description: Marks a texture part: sheet-like detail the 2D draws as `texture` or as open `detail` strokes inside a filled outline (slats, seams, grilles). A texture solid is excluded from the silhouette and cross-scale comparisons and from `volumes-feature`, and belongs only to scales whose 2D draws that texture.

oneOf.description: An ellipsoid centred on the origin of the bone-local frame with the semi-axes radii = [ru, rv, rw] along u, v, w; move it with transform.translation.

oneOf.description: Superelliptic sections joined in order into one skin, at least two, whose centres at give the path. Consecutive sections that overlap, because the path turns back or bends tighter than the section is wide, are reported as volume-loft-fold.

oneOf.description: Superelliptic sections joined in order into one skin, at least two, whose centres at give the path. The order of the sections is the direction of travel; whatever the order, the bends of the path and the handedness of a section rotation, the skin is oriented outward (positive signed volume when both caps are on; with a cap off the tube is open and its faces still look outward). Consecutive sections that overlap, because the path turns back or bends tighter than the section is wide, are reported as volume-loft-fold. AuthoredVolume.description: The handcrafted 3D model of an asset at one preset scale, authored individually against that scale's own 2D shapes (never a filtered copy of another scale): for a printable drawing the smallest modelled feature is the print profile's smallest printable feature at the denominator, a coarser scale is a new abstraction with merged masses, simplified sections and a generalised outline. `body` carries the tone views, `thermal` the thermal model made spatial and `structure` the structural idealisation made spatial. The silhouette of the body in `presentation.defaultPose` agrees with the filled shapes of the representation of the same scale and the bounding box with `dimensions` (validators `volumes-silhouette`, `volumes-bounds`).

denominator.description: The preset scale of this volume; equals its key in `volumes` (validator `volumes-availability`).

body.description: The solids of the body: what the tone views (dark-line, dark-solid, light-line, light-solid) show.

thermal.description: The thermal solids: every thermal region has at least one solid at every authored scale (validator `volumes-thermal-coverage`).

structure.description: The structural solids: every load-bearing bone has a member solid (validator `volumes-structure-coverage`).

decisions.description: The authoring decisions of this scale: what each group of solids stands for, what was merged or simplified against the finer scale and why.

UnavailableVolume.description: A scale without a digital volume. Every authored print drawing requires a volume. A scale below the printable feature size may still have an authored digital model.

ScaleVolume.description: The volume decision for one preset scale: authored or unavailable. A digital model may be authored at a scale without a printable drawing.

Volumes.description: The 3D volumes of an asset, one per preset scale and keyed like `representations`: every scale is authored individually, never derived from another.

Dimensions.description: Nominal overall real dimensions and total mass. The dimensions are the physical envelope of everything that belongs to the asset in its rest pose (held items, attachments, plates, flanges, lids, footings); they exclude stroke width, ground shading, plumes, transport and annotations. A drawing agrees when |measured - declared| <= max(2 % of declared, 15 mm) in every viewpoint.

heightM.description: Extent along world y (up): the vertical extent of the side elevation and of the front elevation.

widthM.description: Extent along world x (ahead): the horizontal extent of the side elevation and of the plan (top view, paper x); the catalog check compares it with the drawn extent. For a side elevation this is the real depth of the object, not its left-right width.

depthM.description: Extent along world z (lateral): the horizontal extent of the front elevation (paper x) and the vertical extent of the plan (top view, paper up); the left-right width of an object drawn in side elevation.

Asset.description: One handcrafted staffage asset; representations decides every preset scale.

volumes.description: The 3D volumes bound to the rig, one individually handcrafted model per preset scale and keyed like `representations`; every authored drawing requires a volume and digital models may also exist below the printable feature size.

powerW.description: Total rated power of all elements in watts, derived from the asset document (powerOf); the asset file is the single source of truth.

CategoryEntry.description: A category of the archive with its folder of asset folders.

MemberEnd.description: An end point of a member: bone-local metres from the origin of its bone at rest.

bone.description: The bone whose frame the point is given in; default the shape's own bone. It is the shape's own bone or one of its ancestors (validator `member-end-not-ancestor`).

x.description: Metres along the bone (u) from its origin at rest.

y.description: Metres along the bone normal (v) from its origin at rest.

z.description: Metres laterally (w, left is +) from its origin at rest; required, never defaulted.

MemberSection.description: The physical section of a member: a rectangle of width w (along bar x bone-w) and height h (completing the orthonormal frame), or a circle of diameter d, all in metres.
